rules_yaml:
title: Exploitation of CVE-2024-35250 via MSKSSRV Kernel Driver
id: fa2d45e4-bef1-44ce-8796-fab83caf1f24
status: experimental
description: Detects exploitation attempts of CVE-2024-35250 by monitoring for process creation involving kernel streaming APIs with malicious IOCTL_KS_PROPERTY requests targeting MSKSSRV driver.
references:
    - https://thehackernews.com/2024/12/cisa-and-fbi-raise-alerts-on-exploited.html
    - https://devco.re/blog/2024/08/23/streaming-vulnerabilities-from-windows-kernel-proxying-to-kernel-part1-en/
    - https://attack.mitre.org/techniques/T1068/
author: Sigma Assistant
date: 2026-09-25
tags:
    - attack.privilege_escalation
    - attack.t1068
logsource:
    category: process_creation
    product: windows
detection:
    selection:
        Image|endswith: '\mskssrv.exe'
        CommandLine|contains:
            - 'IOCTL_KS_PROPERTY'
            - 'KSPROPERTY_TYPE_UNSERIALIZESET'
            - 'KSPROPSETID_DrmAudioStream'
    condition: selection
falsepositives:
    - Legitimate administrative tools using kernel streaming APIs
level: high

title: Privilege Escalation via Kernel Pointer Dereference in MSKSSRV
id: 78d90dda-2f7a-4d58-ade4-f6a8d7646a4d
status: experimental
description: Detects privilege escalation attempts leveraging untrusted pointer dereference vulnerability in MSKSSRV kernel driver through crafted IOCTL_KS_PROPERTY requests.
references:
    - https://thehackernews.com/2024/12/cisa-and-fbi-raise-alerts-on-exploited.html
    - https://devco.re/blog/2024/08/23/streaming-vulnerabilities-from-windows-kernel-proxying-to-kernel-part1-en/
    - https://attack.mitre.org/techniques/T1068/
author: Sigma Assistant
date: 2026-09-25
tags:
    - attack.privilege_escalation
    - attack.t1068
logsource:
    category: process_creation
    product: windows
detection:
    selection:
        Image|endswith:
            - '\cmd.exe'
            - '\powershell.exe'
            - '\wscript.exe'
            - '\cscript.exe'
        CommandLine|contains:
            - 'KsSynchronousIoControlDevice'
            - 'KSPROPSETID_DrmAudioStream'
            - 'KSPROPERTY_TYPE_UNSERIALIZESET'
    condition: selection
falsepositives:
    - Legitimate scripts using kernel streaming APIs
level: high

pipeline.attack_summary: An attacker exploits a local untrusted pointer dereference vulnerability (CVE-2024-35250) in the Microsoft Kernel Streaming Service (MSKSSRV) driver to escalate privileges. The attack leverages IOCTL_KS_PROPERTY with KSPROPERTY_TYPE_UNSERIALIZESET flag, triggering a double-fetch issue that allows arbitrary kernel code execution via crafted input buffers. This enables privilege escalation from user to system level.

indicators.context: Microsoft Windows Kernel-Mode Driver contains an untrusted pointer dereference vulnerability that allows a local attacker to escalate privileges (Patched by Microsoft in June 2024)

Taiwanese cybersecurity company DEVCORE, which discovered and reported CVE-2024-35250, shared additional technical details in August 2024, stating it's rooted in the Microsoft Kernel Streaming Service (MSKSSRV)
ksthunk.sys is the entry point in Kernel Streaming. Its function is quite simple: it converts 32-bit requests from the WoW64 process into 64-bit requests
ks.sys is one of the core components of Kernel Streaming. It is the library of Kernel Streaming responsible for forwarding requests such as IOCTL_KS_PROPERTY to the corresponding device driver

Port class driver mostly used for PCI and DMA-based audio device hardware drivers. Currently, most audio-related processing, such as volume control or microphone-related processing, falls into this category. The main component library used would be portcls.sys

Each of these KS objects will have its own property, and each property corresponds to a specific feature. These properties typically correspond to a set of GUIDs. We can set these properties through IOCTL_KS_PROPERTY

If we give the property set as KSPROPSETID_DrmAudioStream, there is additional processing at [5]. At [6], we can see that it first checks whether Irp->RequestorMode is KernelMode(0). If it is called from user, it will directly return an error

In the IOCTL_KS_PROPERTY of Kernel Streaming, to increase efficiency, KSPROPERTY_TYPE_SERIALIZESET and KSPROPERTY_TYPE_UNSERIALIZESET requests are provided to allow users to operate on multiple properties through a single call
hr = KsOpenDefaultDevice(KSCATEGORY_VIDEO_CAMERA,GENERIC_READ|GENERIC_WRITE, &g_hDevice)

status = KsSynchronousIoControlDevice(CurrentStackLocation->FileObject, 0, CurrentStackLocation->Parameters.DeviceIoControl.IoControlCode, New_KsProperty_req, InSize, OutBuffer, OutSize, &BytesReturned)
When we initially send IOCTL_KS_PROPERTY, we use the existing property KSPROPSETID_Service of MSKSSRV for subsequent operations

However, we will not be explaining these vulnerabilities one by one. Most of these are obvious issues such as unchecked length or index leading to out-of-bounds access. @Fr0st1706 also wrote an exploit for CVE-2024-38054 recently

After re-examining, it was found that IOCTL_KS_PROPERTY uses Neither I/O to transmit data, which means it uses the input buffer for data processing directly. Generally speaking, this method is not recommended as it often leads to double fetch issues. ... From the above figure of KspPropertyHandler, we can see that after the user calls IOCTL, the Type3InputBuffer is directly copied into a newly allocated buffer, containing the KSPROPERTY structure

status: experimental
description: Detects initial access to Mikrotik routers using Winbox Loader to download malicious DLLs such as ipv4.dll, which acts as a downloader for other Slingshot components. This rule targets the primary attack vector involving unauthenticated exploitation of router vulnerabilities.
references:
    - https://securelist.com/apt-slingshot/84312/
    - https://attack.mitre.org/techniques/T1195/
    - https://attack.mitre.org/techniques/T1059/003/

    - attack.t1566.002

    product: windows

rules_yaml:
title: Initial Access via Unauthenticated WAR File Upload
id: 5a8b9c7d-4e2f-1a3b-8c9d-0e1f2a3b4c5d
status: experimental
description: Detects initial access through unauthenticated HTTP POST to webroot directory with crafted WAR archive containing WebShell and payload, leveraging path traversal vulnerability (CWE-22).
references:
    - https://www.sysaid.com/blog/service-desk/on-premise-software-security-vulnerability-notification
    - https://attack.mitre.org/techniques/T1059/001/
    - https://attack.mitre.org/techniques/T1059/003/
    - https://attack.mitre.org/techniques/T1564/003/
    - https://attack.mitre.org/techniques/T1003/001/
    - https://attack.mitre.org/techniques/T1078/002/
    - https://attack.mitre.org/techniques/T1021/001/
    - https://attack.mitre.org/techniques/T1486/
    - https://attack.mitre.org/techniques/T1070/004/
author: Sigma Assistant
date: 2026-09-25
tags:
    - attack.initial-access
    - attack.t1190
    - attack.execution
    - attack.t1059.001
    - attack.t1059.003
    - attack.defense-evasion
    - attack.t1564.003
logsource:
    category: webserver
    product: windows
detection:
    selection:
        request_uri|contains: '/usersfiles'
        request_body|contains: 'usersfiles.war'
    condition: selection
falsepositives:
    - Legitimate administrative uploads to usersfiles directory
level: high

title: Execution of Malicious Loader user.exe via PowerShell
id: 6b7c8d9e-5f2a-3b4c-9d0e-1f2a3b4c5d6e
status: experimental
description: Detects execution of the malicious loader user.exe through PowerShell command line with -WindowStyle Hidden, indicating potential exploitation of CVE-2023-47246 and deployment of GraceWire trojan.
references:
    - https://www.sysaid.com/blog/service-desk/on-premise-software-security-vulnerability-notification
    - https://attack.mitre.org/techniques/T1059/001/
    - https://attack.mitre.org/techniques/T1059/003/
    - https://attack.mitre.org/techniques/T1564/003/
    - https://attack.mitre.org/techniques/T1003/001/
    - https://attack.mitre.org/techniques/T1078/002/
    - https://attack.mitre.org/techniques/T1021/001/
    - https://attack.mitre.org/techniques/T1486/
    - https://attack.mitre.org/techniques/T1070/004/
author: Sigma Assistant
date: 2026-09-25
tags:
    - attack.execution
    - attack.t1059.001
    - attack.t1564.003
logsource:
    category: process_creation
    product: windows
detection:
    selection:
        Image|endswith: '\powershell.exe'
        CommandLine|contains: 'IEX ((new-object net.webclient).downloadstring'
        CommandLine|contains: '-WindowStyle Hidden'
    condition: selection
falsepositives:
    - Legitimate PowerShell scripts using similar patterns for legitimate purposes
level: high

title: Defense Evasion via File Deletion and Log Cleanup
id: 7c8d9e0f-6a3b-4c5d-0e1f-2a3b4c5d6e7f
status: experimental
description: Detects defense evasion techniques used by attacker to remove evidence, including deletion of WAR files and cleanup of log entries using PowerShell scripts.
references:
    - https://www.sysaid.com/blog/service-desk/on-premise-software-security-vulnerability-notification
    - https://attack.mitre.org/techniques/T1059/001/
    - https://attack.mitre.org/techniques/T1059/003/
    - https://attack.mitre.org/techniques/T1564/003/
    - https://attack.mitre.org/techniques/T1003/001/
    - https://attack.mitre.org/techniques/T1078/002/
    - https://attack.mitre.org/techniques/T1021/001/
    - https://attack.mitre.org/techniques/T1486/
    - https://attack.mitre.org/techniques/T1070/004/
author: Sigma Assistant
date: 2026-09-25
tags:
    - attack.defense-evasion
    - attack.t1070.004
logsource:
    category: process_creation
    product: windows
detection:
    selection:
        Image|endswith: '\powershell.exe'
        CommandLine|contains: 'userentry|getLogo\\.jsp|Got\\ LDAP\\ file|ldapSyms|usersfile|time=18686488731'
    condition: selection
falsepositives:
    - Legitimate cleanup scripts using similar patterns
level: high

pipeline.attack_summary: An attacker exploited a path traversal vulnerability (CVE-2023-47246) in SysAid on-premise software to upload a WAR archive containing a WebShell and payload. Post-compromise cleanup was performed using PowerShell scripts that removed evidence from logs and files.

title: Kapeka Backdoor Scheduled Task Creation
rules_yaml:
title: Scheduled Task Creation by Administrator Account
id: c48eae2e-cf13-45f8-8066-335df6870ab5
status: experimental
description: Detects the creation of a scheduled task by administrator account 'dadmin' which may indicate persistence or execution of malicious code.
references:
    - https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/windows/security/threat-protection/auditing/event-4698
    - https://attack.mitre.org/techniques/T1070/001/
    - https://attack.mitre.org/techniques/T1562/002/
author: Sigma Assistant
date: 2026-09-25
tags:
    - attack.persistence
    - attack.execution
    - attack.t1070.001
    - attack.t1562.002
logsource:
    category: process_creation
    product: windows
detection:
    selection:
        CommandLine|contains:
            - 'schtasks.exe'
            - 'taskschd.msc'
        CommandLine|contains:
            - '/create'
            - '/Change'
    selection2:
        CommandLine|contains:
            - '\Microsoft\StartListener'
            - 'dadmin'
    condition: all of selection*
falsepositives:
    - Legitimate administrative scheduled tasks
level: high

    category: process_creation

detection:
    selection:

        CommandLine|contains:
            - '/create'

pipeline.attack_summary: The attack begins with a supply chain compromise where malicious code is inserted into the SolarWinds Orion platform DLL, specifically SolarWinds.Orion.Core.BusinessLayer.dll. This backdoor, known as Sunburst, executes in parallel threads and performs initial reconnaissance to validate the environment before connecting to C2 servers using dynamically generated domains. id: 5a8c7b2f-4d9e-4f1a-9c3d-2e8f1a4b6c7d
status: experimental
description: Detects unauthenticated HTTP POST requests to /json/setup-restore.action with X-Atlassian-Token: no-check header and multipart form data containing a .zip file, indicating exploitation of CVE-2023-22518 for initial access.
references:
    - https://confluence.atlassian.com/security/cve-2023-22518-improper-authorization-vulnerability-in-confluence-data-center-and-server-1311473907.html
    - https://www.huntress.com/blog/confluence-to-cerber-exploitation-of-cve-2023-22518-for-ransomware-deployment
    - https://github.com/ForceFledgling/CVE-2023-22518
    - https://attack.mitre.org/techniques/T1078/004/
author: Sigma Assistant
date: 2026-09-25
tags:
    - attack.initial_access
    - attack.t1078.004
logsource:
    category: webserver
    product: linux-windows/apache-iis
detection:
    selection_method:
        cs-method: POST
    selection_uri:
        cs-uri-query: /json/setup-restore.action
    selection_header:
        cs-header: X-Atlassian-Token: no-check
    selection_content_type:
        cs-header: Content-Type: multipart/form-data
    selection_body:
        cs-body|contains:
            - filename=".*\.zip"
            - buildIndex=true
            - edit=Upload and import
    condition: all of selection_*
falsepositives:
    - Legitimate administrative scripts using the setup-restore endpoint
level: critical

The crafted loader is designed to mimic the legitimate libcurl.dll file by including export function names found in the legitimate version and thus imported by the GUP executable. Only one of the export functions, namely "curl_easy_init" contains malicious code. All other export functions are trivially implemented with "retn 0" instructions. The "curl_easy_init" export function, which implements the malicious code, is the first function from the library that is called by the GUP executable. Therefore, the malicious code is executed immediately when GUP.exe is launched. This unique loader has not been previously seen in FIN7’s attack arsenal, and we are now tracking it as DUBLOADER
